icp.description: Buying committee roles at mid-to-large SEA companies running multi-market customer communications on CPaaS
roles: Head of Customer Communications or CX
icp.company_size: Mid-to-large (500+ employees), operating across 3+ SEA markets

competitor_frame: Regional telco CPaaS arms (e.g. Singtel, AIS, Axiata)
thesis: The primary ICP is the buying committee at mid-to-large SEA companies (fintech, logistics, e-commerce) running high-volume customer communications (OTP, alerts, notifications) across 3+ SEA markets. They evaluate CPaaS on reliability, deliverability, regulatory compliance, and multi-market routing — not on unified-comms features. The engineering lead drives the shortlist; procurement/compliance co-signs on data residency and telco licensing; the CX/comms lead confirms channel coverage.
what_would_prove_this_wrong: If the dominant buying motion is UCaaS/contact-center (not CPaaS API), the ICP shifts to ops/CX leadership, not engineering — and the competitor frame shifts to Zoom, RingCentral, Genesys
If 8x8 wins in SEA primarily through its contact-center bundle rather than standalone CPaaS, the category framing is wrong
If deliverability/OTP reliability is a commodity concern and buyers actually care more about cost arbitrage or developer experience, the deleted reality is different
If the real gating factor is not deliverability but regulatory/data-residency compliance, the ICP and pain map shifts to compliance/legal
vertical_description: Digital banks, payment companies, lending platforms, and insurance tech companies operating across SEA. These companies rely heavily on customer communications for core product flows: OTP for login and transactions, fraud alerts, account balance notifications, KYC verification steps, loan disbursement confirmations. Regulatory requirements (MAS, OJK, BSP) often mandate specific notification formats and audit trails. A failed OTP or missed fraud alert is not a UX inconvenience — it is a compliance event or a direct revenue loss.
